solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Enterprise possibly begins knowing time will run out

indicators.note: a thing that runs out is gone, so the time letter leaves the word for begins

parts.note: begins means starts
hip means knowing or in the know

explanation.surface: A business, once it gets going and knowingly lets time run out, is under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enterprise' is the starship of Star Trek, hence 'possibly'. STARTS loses its T ('will run out') to give STARS.
explanation.definitionFit: The USS Enterprise of Star Trek is a fictional spacecraft, so it is one example of a starship.

clue.text: Son worried being on edge

parts.note: cared can mean worried, as in cared about something

explanation.surface: A boy is anxious, his nerves frayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frightened is jumpy and tense, which is what being on edge describes.

clue.text: Eg, JR Hartley, who we hope would promote a particular POV

definitions.meaning: J R Hartley is the elderly fly-fishing author in a famous British Yellow Pages television advert, so he is an example of a fisherman

definitions.text: who we hope would promote a particular POV
definitions.meaning: an angle is a point of view, so an ..., read whimsically, is someone who pushes an angle

explanation.surface: A fictional fishing author is cast as someone with an agenda to push.
explanation.walkthrough: J R Hartley is from a much-loved British TV advert in which an old man searches bookshops for his own book on fly fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman using rod and line is called by this name, and the second sense plays on angle meaning viewpoint.

clue.text: Flexible dates by express firm

indicators.note: flexible dates are ones that can be moved about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an express train is a fast one, so express gives fast

explanation.surface: A courier company offers delivery dates that can be changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means resolute and unwavering, the sense of firm in standing firm.

clue.text: Inventively signorine tried home building?

indicators.note: doing something inventively means creating a new arrangement, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Some Italian young ladies have had a creative try at something.
explanation.walkthrough: Signorine is the Italian plural of signorina, a young unmarried woman. The definition is cryptic: making up a home's insides, not constructing a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorating and furnishing a room builds up the look of a home, a playful take on construction.

clue.text: Plaster is mostly fixed firm

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: stuck means fixed in place
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A plaster that is largely stuck on firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster or render used to coat walls and mould decoration.

clue.text: Company set up near Los Angeles

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word set is read from the bottom, so backwards

explanation.surface: A business is established close to Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Tesla is the American electric-car maker, so it is an example of a company.

clue.text: Hydrocarbon which becomes cloudier when processed

indicators.note: processing reworks raw material, so the letters of cloudier are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fuel that turns murkier during refining.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum straight from the ground is a mixture of hydrocarbon compounds, so it fits a hydrocarbon.

clue.text: Aged female unable to get along with ex

parts.note: aged means old
lame means unable to walk properly, to get along

explanation.surface: An elderly woman who cannot walk is paired with a former partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A former sweetheart is called by this idiom, which is what an ex is.

clue.text: Le sparadrap ou Band-Aid? It gives life to Caesar, say

definitions.meaning: sparadrap is French for a sticking plaster, so a French word for a wound dressing

definitions.text: It gives life to Caesar, say
definitions.meaning: a salad dressing livens up a salad, and Caesar is a kind of salad

explanation.surface: A French phrase asks about a plaster, then Caesar is revived.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar is a salad here, not the Roman, and 'gives life to' means livens up the flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a vinaigrette for salads, and read literally it is a bandage in the French language.

clue.text: Boost obtained from a ground nutmeg

indicators.note: ground spice is crushed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook gets a lift from some freshly ground spice.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment something is to increase or enlarge it, the verb sense of boost.

clue.text: Reserve, having been given the nod, is saved

parts.note: cued means given a signal, the nod to start

explanation.surface: A substitute player, once signalled to come on, makes a save.
explanation.definitionFit: Rescued means delivered from danger, the sense of saved as a past participle.

clue.text: Chaps getting into editor's change

indicators.note: one thing getting into another goes inside it, so the men go within the editor

parts.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Some men get involved with an editor's alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct or alter it, a specialised sense of change.

clue.text: Learn glib labours — sound somewhat familiar?

indicators.note: letters that labour are worked over, so the letters of learn glib are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to pick up glib talk that seems vaguely familiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'labours' looks like a noun in the surface but is the anagram signal. The question mark marks the pun on 'sound', a bell's chime.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said of something one half remembers, punning on a bell making a noise.

clue.text: Sailor chap I'm winding up in an act of pettiness?

indicators.note: winding something up twists it round, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor teasing a fellow seems petty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding up' reads as teasing in the surface but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochialism is narrow-minded concern with local trivia, a small-mindedness close to pettiness.

clue.text: Fellows who are up working a dice scam

indicators.note: letters that are working are moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dons up late are running a gambling fraud with dice.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage to be 'up' is to be at university, and a fellow is a senior college member.
explanation.definitionFit: University teachers and researchers, the fellows of colleges, are called by this word.

clue.text: Glass vessel

definitions.meaning: a tall glass for sherry or beer
a sailing ship with two or more masts

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a large drinking glass and a fore-and-aft rigged sailing ship.

clue.text: Heads twitch daily

parts.note: domes is slang for heads
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Someone's head twitches every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' in Britain is a cleaner who comes in each day, a domestic help.
explanation.definitionFit: A household servant or cleaner is called a domestic, and a daily is one who comes in by day.

clue.text: Perhaps Cornish treat twerp carelessly cremated

parts.note: a clot is a fool, a twerp

indicators.note: something done carelessly comes out jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An idiot has burnt a West Country dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carelessly' rearranges CREMATED to TEDCREAM. Cornwall is a county in south-west England famous for its cream teas.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick scalded cream is a speciality of Cornwall, eaten with scones, so it is one Cornish treat.

clue.text: Deer displaying natural gift

indicators.note: a container displaying something holds it within, so the doe shows the natural inside

parts.note: a doe is a female deer

explanation.surface: A deer shows off an innate talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gift' is a verb here, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To gift something is to give it away, which is what donating means.

clue.text: Show concerning flesh as food

parts.note: re means concerning, about
veal is calf flesh eaten as meat

explanation.surface: A show on the subject of meat for the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to disclose or make visible, the verb sense of show.

clue.text: Series of six shots? This is too many

parts.note: in cricket an over is a series of six balls bowled
shots of a drug are doses

explanation.surface: A run of six injections is asked about: surely too many?
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six deliveries from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdoses are excessive quantities of a drug, too many doses taken at once.

clue.text: Tendency to split after beginning to dry

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the answer
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a rift is a split

explanation.surface: Something tends to crack once it starts to dry out.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its general direction or trend, a tendency.

clue.text: Earl went on a bike to eat away

parts.note: one rode a bike

explanation.surface: A nobleman cycled off to eat out.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear down gradually, as water and weather eat away rock.

clue.text: What could be flimsy in no good zip?

indicators.note: in puts the flimsy word inside the pair of pieces around it

parts.note: no is taken as written
thin can mean flimsy, as with thin fabric

explanation.surface: A flimsy zip fastener is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' is the definition as American slang for zero, not a fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is informal for zero, none at all, which is what nothing means.

clue.text: I am in front of independent gallery's mirror

indicators.note: in front of puts the first piece ahead of the rest

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone stands before a gallery's looking glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate galleries in London hold British and modern art.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror someone is to copy their actions, the verb sense matching imitate.

clue.text: Repeat ceremony outside English college

indicators.note: one piece outside another wraps round it

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A ceremony held outside an English college is done again.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to say aloud from memory, a way of repeating words.

clue.text: Fragile container? Mine's below

parts.note: egg is old military slang for a mine or bomb, so mine's gives eggs
hell is the place below, the underworld

explanation.surface: A fragile box is mentioned, with someone's mine said to lie underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' is the explosive, not the possessive; 'below' is the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin brittle casing of an egg holds the yolk and white, a delicate holder indeed.
